en: Hetuduka, Upādinnattika (The Dyad on Roots, the Triad on Clung-to)

Dependent on a cause that is both acquired (*upādinna*) and subject to clinging (*upādāniya*), there arises a state that is not a cause (*nahetu*) and is neither acquired nor subject to clinging, by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*)... Under the root condition, there are three; ... [and so on] ... under the non-disappearance condition (*avigatapaccaya*), there are three.

Dependent on a state that is not a cause and is neither acquired nor subject to clinging, there arises a state that is not a cause and is neither acquired nor subject to clinging, by way of the root condition.

Dependent on a cause that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging, there arises a state that is not a cause and is neither acquired nor subject to clinging, by way of the root condition... Under the root condition, there are three; ... [and so on] ... under the non-disappearance condition, there are three.
